reviewed_answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/display-bnpl-messaging describes automatic buy now, pay later messaging and indexes four variant pages for UIKit, SwiftUI, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-16). The April 22 detailed guide shows the client Payment Method Messaging Element for a potential purchase, with a Stripe account, platform SDK preview opt-in, publishable key and test/live key separation. Its examples use amount and currency and allow locale, country and Dashboard payment-method defaults to be overridden (old raw lines 12-26, 71-115, 181-189 and 430-477). UIKit creates and adds a native view asynchronously, SwiftUI exposes loading, loaded, no-content and failure phases with optional manual view data, and Android configures the separate sample messaging SDK and presents Compose Content (old raw lines 90-163, 275-397 and 479-537). These are advertising/display states rather than a financing decision, Intent confirmation or payment result. The existing source-stripe-inapp-display-bnpl-messaging.md preserves most April native mechanics. Its UIKit comment on line 43 overstates .noContent as no eligible BNPL plans for that amount, currency and country. UIKit documents only that this configuration produced no displayable element (old raw lines 124-131). SwiftUI gives below-minimum amount as one possible example, and Android reports no content available (old raw lines 327-334, 385-392 and 502-510). The reciprocal route should preserve that display-state meaning without classifying the customer or financing option as ineligible. Date its three-platform beta scope and distinguish its historical lack of an inline React Native section from the new index route. The November capture supplies no implementation prerequisites for that link.
